Root error boundary belongs in index.tsx / App.tsx, which are owned by another agent — requested in board.md. All localStorage reads in MY files are try/catch-guarded, so they won't be the throw that blanks the app.

Task 2: ChainsBoard adds a window listener for CustomEvent `egregore:concede` that calls moves.concede() when the match is live (!ctx.gameover), feature-detected via `typeof moves.concede === 'function'`, and removes the listener on unmount. The engine owner has already added the move (Game.test.ts exercises it).

Task 3: rebuilt src/Voice.tsx securely with zero backend. On enable it generates a random 32-char [A-Za-z0-9_-] peer id via crypto.getRandomValues and publishes it with moves.announceVoicePeer(peerId) (feature-detected); reads the opponent id from G.voice[opponentID] (feature-detected via `voicePeers` prop defaulting to {}). Only the lower playerID dials, once/if the opponent id is known, re-dialing when the opponent re-announces. The inbound peer.on('call') handler ANSWERS ONLY IF call.peer === G.voice[opponentID], else closes — the H-6 fix. Mute toggle, push-to-talk (hold V), per-call status (mic/connecting/live/opponent-not-in-voice/error), remote volume slider, visible 'opponent in voice' indicator, iOS play-after-gesture, lazy peerjs import, prefs persisted to localStorage with try/catch, full teardown on unmount/disable. Mounted in ChainsBoard for both desktop and phone whenever it is a real two-seat match (matchID && playerID && !isSolo); the old VOICE_CHAT_ENABLED=false gate and 'unsafe, keep unmounted' comments are gone and the security model is documented at the top of Voice.tsx.

Task 4: every WebGL effect I own now cancels rAF on unmount (already did), disposes its GL context via WEBGL_lose_context on unmount (added to Lightfall; Iridescence and SideRays already had it), and pauses rendering while document.hidden (Lightfall guards the render call; Iridescence returns early in its rAF loop; SideRays reschedules the loop at the top then skips the render when hidden so it resumes on show). PixelTrail uses react-three-fiber's <Canvas>, which owns its own context/rAF lifecycle; BorderGlow/ShinyText are CSS/rAF-value animations, not WebGL.
